transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess I'm just having trouble getting things in order lately. My kitchen table is... it's just covered in papers. My husband's appointment papers, church flyers... notes from the senior center, and... half-finished lists. I just... I sit there. I don't know which thing to do first, and... then the whole day is just gone.
Has this kind of difficulty organizing and completing tasks been something you've dealt with since you were younger, or is this a new change for you?

I suppose... it's not a new thing. No. Um... even when I was a little girl, my teachers would write things about it. They'd say I was bright, but... careless. I was always forgetting my books. Or my homework. They always had to remind me to just... finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside. So... yes, I suppose it's always been like this.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?
No... I don't think so. I'm not sad, really. I... I still enjoy my usual things. I just can't always seem to get around to them. But no... I wouldn't say I feel down.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—more days than not—even when there's no clear reason to worry?
No... I don't think so. Just... normal things, I suppose. Not excessively.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

I wouldn't say I'm impulsive, no. But... sitting still... yes, I suppose. Even when I'm trying to sit politely in a meeting or somewhere quiet... I'll catch myself rubbing my hands together. Or tapping my foot. Clicking a pen. I just... shift around a lot. So much that people look over at me sometimes. So, yes... I suppose I do that.

Would you say these difficulties with organization and restlessness cause noticeable problems in more than one area of your life right now — for example, both at home and in social situations or other activities?

Yes... I suppose they do. I... well, I had to give up leading a big event at the senior center recently. I just... couldn't manage it. And at home... my daughter has started double-checking my bills. And my appointments. She... she doesn't really trust that I can keep everything straight on my own anymore. So... yes. It does cause problems.
